**Final search score: 83.5** on the confirm run of `final.py` (the same code scored 86.4 one run earlier). The baseline scores about 1.0. I used **15 of the 24 scorer calls** and about 5½ minutes.

I stopped before the skill's default 15 minutes and 24 calls. The last several candidates were all within the scorer's run-to-run noise of about ±3. I couldn't do the skill's held-out check because I don't have access to the unseen instances.

| | search score |
|---|---|
| baseline | ~1.0 |
| first working version (c1) | 70.7 |
| final pick (c12 → `final.py`) | 86.4, then 83.5 on the confirm run |

**Why it's faster:**
- **Fewer pairs to compare.** The baseline compares every pair of records. The new version orders words from rarest to most common. Two records can only be 80 % alike if they share one of the few rarest words at the start of their lists, so only records that do are compared at all. For example, a 10-word record only needs its rarest 3 words checked.
- **Size filter.** Records whose word counts differ by too much are never compared.
- **Exact duplicates handled once.** Records with the same set of words are grouped first, and their pairs come straight from the group.
- **Short records skipped.** A record with 3 words or fewer can only match a record with exactly the same words, so it skips the comparison step.
- **Words that appear only once** can't link two records, so they never go into the lookup table.
- Every surviving candidate pair is checked with the reference's exact integer test, `5*|A∩B| >= 4*|A∪B|`.

**How I checked correctness:** I compared it against the reference on 40 small random inputs per test run (including empty records, tabs and repeated words) and on large ones of 3,000 records. I also ran 3,000 dense cases with a tiny vocabulary. All matched exactly, with no repeated pairs.

**Candidate log** (scorer scores):
- c1, rare-first prefix filter: 70.7. My first try ordered tied words inconsistently and missed pairs; fixing that made it correct.
- c2, smaller lookup prefix for already-indexed records: 69.2
- c3, small speed-ups: 70.9
- c4, skip records with 3 words or fewer: 76.0
- c5, group identical strings before building word sets: 76.9
- c6, keep words seen only once out of the lookup table: 80.8
- c7, count words with `Counter`: 82.3
- c8, skip too-small candidates by position in the size order: 79.4 and 80.0. My local test said it was faster, so I dropped it on the scorer's verdict.
- c9, a single sort of the vocabulary instead of two: 85.3
- c10, a private `_collections` import: **rejected by the scorer's static check**, which used up one call.
- c11, plain dict counting with no `collections` import: 83.7
- c12, merged lookup and indexing loop: **86.4**, then 83.5 on the confirm run. This is the final pick.
- c13, faster count of once-only words: within noise locally, not scored.

My test and profiling scripts (`harness.py`, `prof*.py`) and the candidate files `c1.py` to `c13.py` are still in the folder.
